lesson_title: Tell the Story of the Problem
hook_text: Five minutes, a cardboard box, and a stall owner in the third row. Here is how a design team wins the room.
clip_script: Do not read your portfolio. Tell it. Thirty seconds: 400 meals a day in polystyrene, 63 boxes in one drain on a Monday, one photo. Then the brief and the four rules that mattered. Then both sketches held up and why you chose. Then the drawings on the board and the model into the front row, with the moment it went wrong and the fix. Then the longest part, ninety seconds: the evaluation. Passes short, fails long, with the cause and the fix, finger on the rib: buckled at fourteen. Back to the brief: less harm by how much, benefit kept, your own footprint named. Numbered recommendations. Questions: hear it, repeat it, answer with evidence, and if you do not know, say so and say how you would find out. Everyone speaks. Name your weakness before they do, and you own the room.
visual_style: Whiteboard timeline of six blocks sized by seconds; a photo of a drain; two sketches held up; a model passed hand to hand; a results table with one highlighted fail; a question mark answered with a scale icon.
pacing: The story opening, the six blocks, the fail owned, the question rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and time your team's opening thirty seconds tonight.
